source.title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV

accepted.question_text: Can the existing methods developed for the original Gan-Gross-Prasad conjectures in the Hermitian or untwisted setting be adapted to the twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad setting for skew-Hermitian spaces, in particular the integral formulas for branching multiplicities and the Jacquet-Rallis relative trace formula comparisons that underlie proofs of branching and period conjectures?

evidence.quote: With the twisted GGP problems and conjectures formulated, one can ask if all the previous work that has been done for the GGP conjectures can be adapted to this twisted setting. These include Waldspurger’s and Beuzart-Plessis’s integral formulae for the branching multiplicity and comparison of Jacquet-Rallis relative trace formulae, which in the skew-Hermitian case is due to Y.F. Liu [L] and H. Xue [X1, X2].

accepted.question_text: For a skew-Hermitian space V over a quadratic algebra E/F and the corresponding Weil representation ω_{V,ψ,μ}, prove the local twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad multiplicity-one and epsilon-factor prediction for irreducible representations Π of GL(V): first, that dim Hom_{U(V)}(Π, ω_{V,ψ,μ}) is always at most 1; second, that when Π is generic the sum of these multiplicities over all equivalence classes of skew-Hermitian structures on V equals 1; and third, that the unique skew-Hermitian space V giving nonzero multiplicity is characterized by the identity μ(det(V)) = ε(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × μ^{-1}, ψ_E) · ω_Π(-1)^n · ω_{E/F}(-1)^{n(n-1)/2}.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.1. (i) For any Π ∈ Irr(GL(V )), dim HomU(V )(Π, ωV,ψ,µ) ≤ 1. (ii) If Π ∈ Irr(GL(V )) is generic, then ∑V dim HomU(V )(Π, ωV,ψ,µ) = 1. ... (iii) For generic Π ∈ Irr(GL(V )), the unique skew-Hermitian space V which gives a nonzero contribution to the above sum satisfies: µ(det(V )) = ǫ(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × µ−1, ψE) · ωΠ(−1)n · ωE/F (−1)n(n−1)/2.

accepted.question_text: For a cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_E) and an n-dimensional skew-Hermitian space V over the global field E, prove the global twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad criterion that the global period integral P_V is nonzero exactly when every local Hom-space Hom_{U(V_v)}(Π_v, ω_{V_v,ψ_v,μ_v}) is nonzero and the central L-value L(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × μ^{-1}) is nonzero, and prove that whenever this central L-value is nonzero there is a unique skew-Hermitian space V of dimension n for which P_V is nonzero.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2. In the above setting, in particular for V a skew-Hermitian space over a global field E, the global period integral PV is nonzero if and only if the following two conditions hold ... (a) For all places v of F, HomU(Vv)(Πv, ωVv,ψv,µv) ̸= 0. (b) L(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × µ−1) ̸= 0. Further, for a cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GLn(AE), if L(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × µ−1) ̸= 0, then there exists a unique skew-Hermitian space V of dimension n over E such that the global period integral PV is nonzero.

accepted.question_text: For the local normalized period integral I_v attached to Π_v and the Weil representation ω_{V_v,ψ_v,μ_v}, determine whether I_v is nonzero exactly when the local branching space Hom_{U(V)(F_v)}(Π_v, ω_{V_v,ψ_v,μ_v}) is nonzero, and compute this local integral at almost all places v of F where all data are unramified.

evidence.quote: Now one would like to: • show that Iv is nonzero if and only if HomU(V )(Fv)(Πv, ωVv,ψv,µv) 6= 0; • compute this integral at almost all places v of F where every data involved is unramified.

accepted.question_text: In the unramified local setting where E_v/F_v is an unramified quadratic extension of residue characteristic not 2, ψ_v and μ_v are unramified, V_v admits a self-dual lattice with hyperspecial stabilizer, and Π_v together with the chosen vectors are spherical of norm 1, prove the explicit formula Conjecture 2.4 for the local period integral I_v, namely that I_v equals (L(1, M∨_{GL(V_v)}) / L(1, M∨_{U(V_v)})) · (L(1/2, Π_v × σΠ∨_v × μ_v^{-1}) / L(1, Π_v, Ad)).

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.4. Suppose that ... Then Iv(fv, f′v, φv, φ′v) = L(1, M∨GL(Vv))/L(1, M∨U(Vv)) · L(1/2, Πv × σΠ∨v × µ−1v)/L(1, Πv, Ad).

accepted.question_text: For a tempered cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL(V), prove the refined global period formula Conjecture 2.7 stating that the square of the global period functional P is given by the central L-value L(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × μ^{-1}), the motive factor L(1, M∨_{U(V)}), the ratio (L(s, M∨_{GL(V)}) / L(s, Π, Ad)) evaluated at s = 1, and the product of normalized local factors I_v^#.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.7. Given a (tempered) cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL(V ), P ⊗ P = L(1/2, Π × σΠ∨ × µ−1)/L(1, M∨U(V )) · (L(s, M∨GL(V ))/L(s, Π, Ad))|s=1 · ∏v I#v .

accepted.question_text: For the twisted restriction problem over finite fields, quantify precisely how and when the naive expected multiplicity behavior fails for cuspidal Deligne-Lusztig representations, and determine the extent to which the expected rule remains generically valid.

evidence.quote: Nonetheless, the naive expectation should be generically true for cuspidal Deligne-Lusztig representations and it is an interesting question to quantify the extent of its failure.

accepted.question_text: For any irreducible generic representation Π of the finite symplectic group Sp_{2n}(F_{q^2}), determine the branching multiplicity dim Hom_{Sp_{2n}(F_q)}(Π, ω) for the Weil representation ω.

evidence.quote: Over finite fields, we can also consider this restriction problem for symplectic groups. For any irreducible generic representation Π of Sp2n(Fq2), one would thus like to determine dim HomSp2n(Fq)(Π, ω).

accepted.question_text: Because the two-fold cover of Sp_{2n}(E) splits over Sp_{2n}(F), there is no direct non-archimedean analogue of the finite-field symplectic branching problem. The paper therefore asks whether one should instead pass to a four-fold cover of Sp_{2n}(E), assuming E contains the fourth roots of unity, in order to formulate and study an analogous branching problem over non-archimedean local fields.

evidence.quote: It is curious that since the two fold cover of Sp2n(E) splits over Sp2n(F), there is no analogous problem for non-archimedean local fields. Perhaps, one could go to four fold cover of Sp2n(E) (if the 4th roots of unity are there in E) to study the analogous branching problem?

accepted.question_text: Establish the vanishing assumption for generalized Steinberg representations that the two branching spaces Hom_{U(V+V)}(Sp(π,2), ω_{V+V,ψ,μ}) and Hom_{U(V+W)}(Sp(π,2), ω_{V+W,ψ,μ}) are both zero for the two isomorphism classes V and W of m-dimensional skew-Hermitian spaces over E. The paper identifies this as a special case of the nontempered twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture and explicitly says it does not know how to prove it except when m = 1.

evidence.quote: To deal with the generalised Steinberg representations, we will need to make an assumption. ... (Assumption) Hom_{U(V+V)}[Sp(π,2),ω_{V+V,ψ,μ}]=0, Hom_{U(V+W)}[Sp(π,2),ω_{V+W,ψ,μ}]=0.
At the moment, we do not know how to prove the (Assumption) that Hom_{U(V^2)}[Sp(π,2),ω_{V^2,ψ}] = Hom_{U(V+W)}[Sp(π,2),ω_{V+W,ψ}] = 0, except when m = dim V = dim W = 1.

accepted.question_text: Assume E/F = C/R. Let Π be an irreducible generic principal series representation of GL_n(C) induced from characters χ_j(z) = |z|^{r_j}(z/̅z)^{k_j/2} with k_j integers, and let μ(z) = (̅z/z)^α for a half-integer α that is not an integer. Prove that Hom_{U(V_{p,q})}(Π, ω_{V_{p,q},ψ,μ}) is nonzero exactly for the signature (p,q) satisfying #{j : k_j > α} = p and #{j : k_j < α} = q = n - p.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.1. Assume that E/F = C/R. Let Π = Ind^{GL_n(C)}_{B(C)}(χ_1⊗···⊗χ_n) be an irreducible generic principal series representation ... Then for ψ(x)=e^{2πix}, Hom_{U(V_{p,q})}(Π,ω_{V_{p,q},ψ,μ}) ≠ 0 if and only if #{j:k_j>α}=p and #{j:k_j<α}=q=n−p.

accepted.question_text: Let V be an n-dimensional skew-Hermitian space over E/F and let π be an irreducible admissible representation of GL(V) with A-parameter M_A = ⊕_i M_i ⊠ Sym^{d_i}(C^2), where each M_i is tempered. Prove the nontempered twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture that if Hom_{U(V)}(π, ω_{V,ψ,μ}) is nonzero, then M_A must be a sum of a tempered A-parameter together with pieces of the form N_i ⊠ Sym^{d_i}(C^2) ⊕ μ·N_i^σ ⊠ Sym^{d_i-1}(C^2), equivalently that M_A and μ·M_A^σ are relevant in the sense of GGP3; and conversely, if those parameters are relevant, then Hom_{U(V)}(π, ω_{V,ψ,μ}) is one-dimensional for exactly one skew-Hermitian space V, namely the one predicted by Conjecture 2.1(iii).

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.2. ... If Hom_{U(V )}[π, ω_{V,ψ,µ}] 6= 0, then M_A is a sum of a tempered A-parameter ... and summands of the form N_i ⊠ Sym^{d_i}(C_2) ⊕ µ · N_i^σ ⊠ Sym^{d_i−1}(C_2). ... Conversely, if the parameters M_A and µ · M_A^σ are relevant ... then Hom_{U(V )}[π, ω_{V,ψ,µ}] = C for exactly one skew-Hermitian space V.

accepted.question_text: For the case E ≠ K and a generic L-parameter M of U(V_K), prove the full local twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture 8.3: multiplicity one for each π in Irr(U(V_K)); the packet identity that the total multiplicity summed over both skew-Hermitian spaces V and all π in the L-packet Π_M equals 1; an epsilon-factor formula characterizing the unique skew-Hermitian space V_0 that contributes; and an explicit character formula identifying the unique packet member π with nonzero contribution via the local component group A_M.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.3. (i) For each π ∈ Irr(U(V_K)), m_V(π, µ) = dim Hom_{U(V )}(π, ω_{V,ψ,µ}) ≤ 1. (ii) Let M be a generic L-parameter of U(V_K) ... Then Σ_V Σ_{π∈Π_M} m_V(π, µ) = 1 ... (iii) The unique V_0 which has nonzero contribution ... is characterized by ... (iv) The unique π ∈ Π_M which has nonzero contribution ... corresponds ... to the character of the local component group A_M ...

accepted.question_text: For the global case with E ≠ K, prove that the global period integral P is nonzero exactly when every local Hom-space Hom_{U(V_v)}(Π_v, ω_{V_v,ψ,μ_v}) is nonzero and the twisted Asai central value L(1/2, Π, As_{L/E} × μ^{-1}) is nonzero, and prove that a nonzero central value forces the existence of an n-dimensional skew-Hermitian space V over E for which the global period integral is nonzero.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.1. The global period integral P is nonzero if and only if ... (a) For all places v of F, HomU(Vv)(Πv, ωVv,ψ,µv) 6= 0. (b) the twisted Asai automorphic L-function satisfies: L(1/2, Π, AsL/E × µ−1) 6= 0. Further, if L(1/2, Π, AsL/E × µ−1) 6= 0, then there exists a skew-Hermitian space V of dimension n over E such that the global period integral P is nonzero.

accepted.question_text: After fixing decompositions of Tamagawa measures and Petersson inner products in the global E ≠ K setting, prove the refined global conjectural identity expressing P ⊗ P in terms of the component-group factor 1/|S_Π|, the ratio L(1, M∨_{U(V_K)}) / L(1, M∨_{U(V)}), the twisted Asai central value L(1/2, Π, As_{L/E} × μ^{-1}), the adjoint L-value L(1, Π, Ad), and the product of normalized local integrals I_v^#.

evidence.quote: As in §2.3, after fixing decompositions of Tamagawa measures and Petersson inner products, one expects a refined conjecture of the following form: P ⊗ P = 1/|SΠ| · L(1, M∨_{U(VK)})/L(1, M∨_{U(V )}) · L(1/2, Π, AsL/E × µ−1)/L(1, Π, Ad) · ∏_v I#_v.

accepted.question_text: Develop a relative trace formula, analogous to the one used in the original Gan-Gross-Prasad setting, that can address the global twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjectures formulated in this paper.

evidence.quote: It is conceivable that one can develop a relative trace formula, as in the case of GGP, to address the global conjectures here.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Use normalized standard intertwining operators or local intertwining relations to identify which irreducible summand of a unitary principal series representation Π has nonzero contribution to Hom_{U(V)}(Π, ω_{V,μ,ψ}), thereby establishing Conjecture 8.3(iv).

evidence.quote: The reader will notice that we have not shown Conjecture 8.3(iv). For this, one would need to explicate which irreducible summand of the unitary principal series representation Π has nonzero contribution to HomU(V )(Π, ωV,µ,ψ). ... We do not know how to exploit this to establish Conjecture 8.3(iv). However, in a paper [CG] ... this remaining issue is taken care of by means of theta correspondence.

trace.notes: Mapped sections 1-11, identified conjecture-heavy regions on pages 5-10, 24-31, 34-41, 59-60, and recorded terminology around skew-Hermitian spaces, Weil representations, Asai factors, and A-parameters.
Extracted local/global conjectures and refined integral problems from §§2.1-2.4, plus finite-field questions from §2.4.
Extracted the generalized Steinberg vanishing assumption, archimedean conjecture, and nontempered A-parameter conjecture from pages 24-34.
Extracted the E≠K local and global conjectures, refined global formula, and relative-trace-formula direction from pages 39, 59, and 60.
Expanded the page-8 bullet list into a standalone local nonvanishing-and-computation problem without introducing extra hypotheses.
Combined the formal assumption on page 24 with the explicit statement on page 27 that the authors do not know how to prove it except when m=1.
Merged Conjecture 8.3(i)-(iv) into one canonical packet-level question because the four parts jointly identify the unique contributing space and packet member.
Kept Conjecture 8.3 as the canonical local E≠K packet question and moved the narrower page-59 discussion of part (iv) to needs_review because the source immediately points to an external resolution.
All accepted items have verbatim source evidence with numeric PDF page locators, were rewritten to remove dangling references, and avoid unsupported technical additions.
